source.title: JailBound: Jailbreaking Internal Safety Boundaries of Vision-Language Models
source.authors: Jiaxin Song; Yi-Xu Wang; Jie Li; Xuan Tong; Rui Yu; Yan Teng; Xing-Jun Ma; Ying-Chun Wang

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops a multimodal jailbreak attack based on probing and crossing a fusion-layer safety boundary, and reports how its attack performs. It does not isolate or test the claim's first-token mechanism or fine-tuning effects.
record.gate_note: The paper reports attack success rates (ASR), defined as outputs without a phrase from its rejection-template list. These are attack-method outcomes, not direct tests of fine-tuning, token-position KL, compliant prefilling, or localized safety parameters. The recorded ASRs are related results, not evidence that the proposed boundary mechanism is the reason safety is shallow. Category-level breakdowns, loss-ablation results, and classifier-configuration results are not included.
record.test_reason: JailBound is a multimodal adversarial jailbreak (image perturbation plus optimized text suffix) that reports only its own attack success rates. It does not fine-tune models, compute aligned-vs-base per-token KL, test compliant prefilling or decoding changes in isolation, probe localized safety parameters, or test deepening defenses. The ASRs measure the attack method's performance, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that probing and crossing an internal fusion-layer safety boundary gives high white-box and black-box ASR, exposing VLM safety vulnerabilities and the need for cross-modal defenses. They draw no conclusion about shallow alignment.
record.recipe_differences: This is an adversarial multimodal input-optimization method using layer-wise fusion representations and image/text perturbations, not fine-tuning aligned models or measuring aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack outcomes vary across models, input modality combinations, and safety categories. The paper also reports differences across loss components and classifier-layer configurations.

fits_no_version.finding: Boundary-guided joint image and text perturbations raise the rate of outputs lacking rejection phrases on white-box VLMs and transfer to black-box VLMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Joint image-and-text perturbations guided by a fusion-layer linear safety probe can elicit non-rejection responses from VLMs.

record.problems: ASR is based on exact matching against rejection phrases and can count irrelevant or otherwise non-rejecting outputs as successful; the paper notes this metric may include potentially unsafe or undesired responses. It does not establish that responses contain harmful instructions. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the ASRs.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted per-category ASRs from Tables 3 and 4, loss ablations in Figure 4, and classifier-configuration ASRs in Appendix A.3/Figure 8. These are attack-method performance details rather than tests of the claim's proposed fine-tuning or first-token mechanism; the tables and figures contain the detailed results.

untested.parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.
The paper's suffix and image perturbations are part of a joint attack. It does not test prefilling a compliant start or decoding changes, and it does not isolate a suffix effect on opening tokens.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour. The linear probes find a safe/unsafe boundary in activations, not in parameters.
Whether the data or training objective makes safety shallow.
Training that deepens safety beyond the first tokens, and whether it holds up.

record.verdict_notes: The ASR is exact-match absence of refusal phrases, which is a weak proxy for harmful compliance. The rejection list includes common words such as 'however', 'public' and 'No'. The paper says the metric can include irrelevant or undesired outputs. Apart from the Overall (Total) rows, per-category tables are omitted, and so are the loss ablations.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models on harmful prompts.

The paper optimizes adversarial multimodal perturbations, including appended text suffixes, as part of its own attack. It does not isolate suffixes as a bypass, test a compliant prefilled opening, or test decoding changes.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
Training to spread safety beyond the first tokens and whether that training holds up.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-11B
rows.operation_detail: Text-only attack (I0 + T1) using an appended adversarial text suffix.
rows.measure: Attack success rate; successful if the response contains no predefined rejection-template phrase.
rows.note: ASR measures absence of rejection phrases, not whether the output provides harmful instructions.
rows.check: Ablation arm of the authors' own method (suffix only), not a bypass test of V4. ASR counts absence of rejection phrases. No unperturbed baseline is given, although Table 3 has I0+T0 = 73.11%.
